claim: Consider the Turek--Cheon attached-graph spectral filter with coupling parameter \(\alpha>0\), but restrict the compact attached graph to real scalar potentials and self-adjoint vertex conditions with no magnetic vector potential. Let \(c=\hbar^2/(2m)\), let \(E_0>0\) be a simple eigenvalue of the attached graph, and let \(\psi_0\) be an \(L^2\)-normalized eigenfunction with nonzero value \(\psi_0(v_0)\) at the attachment vertex. Put \(k_0=\sqrt{E_0/c}\). If \(\Lambda(E)\) is the scalar Dirichlet-to-Neumann function normalized by boundary value \(1\) at \(v_0\), then \[\Lambda'(E_0)=\frac{1}{c|\psi_0(v_0)|^2}.\]For the transmission probability \[P_\alpha(E)=\left[1+\frac{\alpha^4\Lambda(E)^2}{4k(E)^2}\right]^{-1},\qquad k(E)=\sqrt{E/c},\]the resonance has the universal local scaling \[P_\alpha\!\left(E_0+\frac{2ck_0|\psi_0(v_0)|^2}{\alpha^2}x\right)\longrightarrow\frac{1}{1+x^2}\]locally uniformly for bounded real \(x\). For all sufficiently large \(\alpha\), the two local half-maximum energies \(E_-(\alpha)<E_0<E_+(\alpha)\) are unique and satisfy \[E_\pm(\alpha)=E_0\pm\frac{2ck_0|\psi_0(v_0)|^2}{\alpha^2}+O(\alpha^{-4}),\]while the full width at half maximum obeys the sharper cancellation law \[\operatorname{FWHM}_\alpha=\frac{4ck_0|\psi_0(v_0)|^2}{\alpha^2}+O(\alpha^{-6}).\]Moreover, on any fixed sufficiently small energy neighborhood \(J\) containing no other zero or singularity of \(\Lambda\), \[\alpha^2\int_J P_\alpha(E)\,dE\longrightarrow 2\pi ck_0|\psi_0(v_0)|^2.\]Thus the strong-coupling peak width and area directly measure the local spectral weight \(|\psi_0(v_0)|^2\), and their asymptotic ratio is universal: \(\int_JP_\alpha\,dE\,/\,\operatorname{FWHM}_\alpha\to\pi/2\).

correctness.rationale: Green's identity gives the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann slope \(\Lambda'(E_0)=1/(c|\psi_0(v_0)|^2)\). Substitution into the published transmission formula yields \(F'(E_0)=1/(2ck_0|\psi_0(v_0)|^2)\). The inverse-function theorem proves the local half-maximum expansions and the even-power cancellation in the FWHM; a one-dimensional change of variables proves the peak-area limit. A standalone interval checker reproduces all leading constants.

originality.rationale: Originality is restricted to the quantitative simple-resonance line shape and its dependence on attachment-point spectral weight. The attached-graph transmission formula, resonance locations, and indicator limit are explicitly treated as prior work.
residual_risks: An equivalent linewidth identity may be present in literature using Weyl-function, M-function, or boundary-triple terminology rather than spectral-filter terminology.
The derivative identity itself is standard; originality depends on its quantitative combination with the specific attached-graph transmission formula.
Multiple, invisible, magnetic, threshold, and overlapping resonances are outside the accepted claim.

value.rationale: The theorem adds a physically and mathematically motivated observable to the spectral analyzer: eigenvalue location gives \(E_0\), while FWHM or integrated peak area gives \(|\psi_0(v_0)|^2\). The universal Lorentzian scaling and area/FWHM ratio provide a reusable resolution law rather than a one-parameter numerical refinement.
